title: Check your understanding: Quality Dimensions & Metadata

items.prompt: Why can simple syntactic schema validation fail to catch severe semantic accuracy defects like an extra trailing zero in a transaction ledger?
choices: Because floating-point numbers cannot be stored in computer memory
Because the corrupted number remains a syntactically valid positive float, even though it distorts the true distribution
Because databases automatically round all numbers to zero
Because semantic errors only occur in unstructured text datasets
items.explain: A value like $15,000.00 is syntactically a valid positive float. Naive type checking cannot know the true intended purchase was $1,500.00 without statistical outlier screening.

items.prompt: What missingness mechanism is present when high-income survey respondents systematically refuse to disclose their salary?
items.explain: When the probability of a value being missing depends directly on the unobserved missing value itself (e.g. concealing extreme income), the mechanism is Missing Not at Random (MNAR).

items.prompt: Under the FAIR data principles, what does the acronym stand for?
items.explain: The FAIR principles require scientific datasets to be Findable (persistent IDs), Accessible (standard protocols), Interoperable (standard schemas/ontologies), and Reusable (clear licensing).

items.prompt: Dropping rows with missing values is always safe in healthcare datasets because clinical lab tests are missing completely at random.
items.explain: Missing clinical measurements are rarely MCAR; doctors order tests selectively based on patient condition. Dropping missing rows severely biases models toward critically ill patients.

items.prompt: How does inconsistent date formatting (e.g., mixing US MM/DD/YYYY and European DD/MM/YYYY) corrupt machine learning models?
items.rubric: Causes chronological disordering, leading to temporal data leakage across train/validation splits.
items.sample_answer: Inconsistent date conventions cause chronological sorting errors, which misplaces records and risks leaking future information into past training features.
